item.title: Go Daily Question 220
item.description:
How should parts A and B in the code below be modified so that it compiles successfully?

func main() {
	var m map[string]int        //A
	m["a"] = 1 
	if v := m["b"]; v != nil {  //B
		fmt.Println(v)
	}
}
func main() {
	m := make(map[string]int)
	m["a"] = 1
	if v,ok := m["b"]; ok {
		fmt.Println(v)
	}
}
🔑 Solution Analysis:

At A, only the map m is declared without allocating memory space, so it cannot be assigned directly. You need to use make(). It is recommended to initialize a map directly using make() or a composite literal.

item.title: Go Daily Question 172
item.description:
How many syntax issues are there in the following code, and what are they?

package main
import (
    "fmt"
)
func main() {
    var x string = nil
    if x == nil {
        x = "default"
    }
    fmt.Println(x)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis: 
./prog.go:8:17: cannot use nil as string value in variable declaration
./prog.go:9:10: invalid operation: x == nil (mismatched types string and untyped nil)

var x string = nil Error

In Go, the zero value for a string type is an empty string "", not nil. nil is typically used for types like pointers, slices, maps, channels, and interfaces. Therefore, assigning nil to a string type variable x will result in a compilation error.

item.title: Go Daily Question 157
item.description:
How should A and B in the following code be modified to compile successfully?

func main() {
    var m map[string]int        //A
    m["a"] = 1
    if v := m["b"]; v != nil {  //B
        fmt.Println(v)
    }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

// A At point A, map m is only declared, and no memory space is allocated. Writing to an uninitialized map will cause a panic.

Therefore, var m map[string]int needs to be changed to m := make(map[string]int).

item.title: Go Daily Question 141
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {
    s := make(map[string]int)
    delete(s, "h")
    fmt.Println(s["h"])
}
  • A. runtime panic
  • B. 0
  • C. compilation error
🔑 Answer Analysis:

B Run online Deleting a non-existent key does not cause a panic.

Extended Question

In this problem, s is already initialized. Would the behavior be the same if it were uninitialized?

item.title: Go Daily Question 132
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type person struct {  
    name string
}

func main() {  
    var m map[person]int
    p := person{"mike"}
    fmt.Println(m[p])
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: 0

Uninitialized map: reads zero value, writes panic.

item.title: Go Daily Question 061
item.description:
Two problems at once, because they are related.

  1. What is the output of the following code?
package main

import (
    "fmt"
)

func main() {
    a := []int{2: 1}
    fmt.Println(a)
}

A: Compilation error; B: [2 1]; C: [0 0 1]; D: [0 1]

  1. What is the output of the following code?
package main

func main() {
    var x = []int{4: 44, 55, 66, 1: 77, 88}
    println(len(x), x[2])
}

A: 5 66; B: 5 88; C: 7 88; D: None of the above

item.title: Go Daily Question 050
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {  
    s := make(map[string]int)
    delete(s, "h")
    fmt.Println(s["h"])
}

A. runtime panic B. 0 C. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

B 0 Deleting a non-existent key will not cause a panic. Outputting a non-existent key will return the zero value of its type.

Extension:

func main() {
    var s map[string]int
    delete(s, "h")
    s["h"] = 1
    fmt.Println(s["h"])
}

Deleting from a nil map will also not panic. However, writing to a nil map will panic.

item.title: Go Daily Question 049
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

func main() {  
    var i interface{}
    if i == nil {
        fmt.Println("nil")
        return
    }
    fmt.Println("not nil")
}

A. nil B. not nil C. compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

A For an interface type, the value is nil only when both its dynamic value and dynamic type are nil.

item.title: Go Daily Question 040
item.description:
What is the output of the following code?

type person struct {  
    name string
}

func main() {  
    var m map[person]int
    p := person{"mike"}
    fmt.Println(m[p])
}

A.0 B.1 C.Compilation error

🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: A 0

m is a map, and its value is nil. Getting a value from a nil map will not cause an error; instead, it returns the corresponding zero value. Here, the value is of type int, so it returns 0.
